title: Send Message Error. Insufficient certificate transparency. Cannot see to override
creator: sj+mozilla
content:
Hello Community and Volunteers.

Thank you in advance for offering your time and energy.

I have been using and relying upon Thunderbird for decades and do my best to donate on a semi-regular basis to help keep the project alive.

Recently I began to receive the following error message when sending email:

"Sending of the message failed. The server presented insufficient certificate transparency information. Its certificate may not have been publicly disclosed, and it may have been misissued. The configuration related to mail.lu**********gn.com.au must be corrected."

I had not changed anything on the server or any settings in Thunderbird. It's probably useful to explain the I have never had any issues sending email that weren't directly related to password issues.

I have tried the following in Thunderbird.

1. Purging server certificates 2. Switching between SMTP port 587 and 465

Please note that receiving email still works fine.

I use an android email app called FairEmail (great email app), which still allows me to send email through the effected domain SMTP email server. I am guessing this may be because although I use STARTTLS on port 587, I have FairEmail set to fallback to "insecure connections" as a last ditch resort to allow sending when secure options fail.

Hope this provides a good background to begin helping. Let me know if I have missed something important.

Warm wishes, Steve

Not sure why as this is only recently started to happen.

The full message is:

Sending of the message failed. An error occurred while sending mail. The mail server responded: Policy-DT52 Message permanently rejected - Policy violation.. Please check the message and try again.

I found if I put the web site as follows it will go through:

Which I can't understand.

Anyone have some thoughts on this?

Thank you Peter
